prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in the streamable-http client's `post_writer` task: it is spawned with `tg.start_soon()` and the caller proceeds to yield the session before `post_writer` has actually entered its stream context and started consuming from `write_stream_reader`, so early writes/messages can be lost or reordered. members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in the streamable-http client's `post_writer` task: it is spawned with `tg.start_soon()` and the caller proceeds to yield the session before `post_writer` has actually entered its stream context and started consuming from `write_stream_reader`, so early writes/messages can be lost or reordered. members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in the streamable-http client's `post_writer` task: it is spawned with `tg.start_soon()` and the caller proceeds to yield the session before `post_writer` has actually entered its stream context and started consuming from `write_stream_reader`, so early writes/messages can be lost or reordered. Both PRs fix this identically: they add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the relevant `async with` block, enabling the caller to use `tg.start()` and block until `post_writer` is actually ready.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs target the same #2431 unpickling TypeError on MCPError subclasses. #2555's __reduce__ is hand-written only on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so any other current or future MCPError subclass with a constructor signature that doesn't match (code, message, data) is left with the identical bug. #2478 fixes it once at the MCPError base class via a generic _restore_mcp_error dispatcher (from_error_data for the general case, from_error specifically for UrlElicitationRequiredError), so it covers the same UrlElicitationRequiredError case #2555 fixes plus every other subclass, and removes the '# pragma: no cover' on MCPError.data showing the shared path is now actually exercised in tests. Recommend closing #2555 in favor of #2478's broader base-class fix, but port over #2555's test cases for UrlElicitationRequiredError specifically (pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(...)) round-trip preserving elicitations/message) into #2478 before merging, since #2478's shown diff doesn't include test file changes.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: MCPError-family exceptions fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args (set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__) doesn't match subclass constructor signatures — concretely raising TypeError on UrlElicitationRequiredError (tracked as #2431). PR #2555 attacks it locally: adds __reduce__ only to UrlElicitationRequiredError, reconstructing from (self._elicitations, self.message). PR #2478 attacks it at the root: adds a module-level _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher that special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (via from_error) and falls back to the generic MCPError.from_error_data for every other subclass, and drops the '# pragma: no cover' on MCPError.data — implying a new base-class __reduce__ now exercises that property on every pickle round-trip, not just this one subclass. (2 PRs)
